newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan takes low-key stance after islands showdown.
newsitem.headline: Japan takes low-key stance after islands showdown.

text.p: Japan took a low-key posture towards its dispute over East China Sea islands on Tuesday, the day after Tokyo's coast guard thwarted an attempted landing by a flotilla of Chinese nationalists.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto declined to comment on Tokyo's deployment of 60 patrol ships to keep a 20-boat flotilla of Chinese nationalists away from the islets, held by Japan as the Senkakus but claimed by Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
Transport Minister Makoto Koga, whose ministry oversees the Maritime Safety Agency (MSA), Japan's coast guard, thanked the agency for preventing the landing and avoiding injuries or incidents.

"I feel great regret that they entered Japan's territorial waters. But I want to thank the Maritime Safety Agency and other parties concerned for blocking their (Chinese activists) landing on the isles," Koga told a regularly scheduled news conference.

The minister supported the MSA's action in temporarily detaining, but not arresting, several activists who leapt aboard an MSA patrol boat when it bumped into their vessel in what appeared to be attempts to incite embarrassing confrontations.
"Our policing was appropriately carried out," Koga said.
Japan's mixture of firmness and restraint, judged a success by analysts in Taiwan and Hong Kong, drew sharp criticism from a Japanese daily newspaper that espouses nationalist causes.
"Japan should have seized the ships and arrested the activists immediately," the arch-conservative Sankei Shimbun newspaper said in an editorial on Tuesday.

"Our country must make clear how it thinks about the Senkaku Islands and take strong action by seizing ships and arresting those for invading our territorial waters or illegally landing on the islands."
Japan's claim to the islands has fuelled nationalist passion in Chinese communities in Hong Kong, Taiwan and North America since Japanese rightists built a lighthouse there in July 1996.
